title: Dodge Ramcharger (first generation)
verdict: Dodge showed up late to the full-size 4x4 party, then walked in with full-time four-wheel drive, a 440 and a roof you could unbolt and leave in the garage. It's the big, loud, slightly forgotten member of the Bronco–Blazer–Scout gang, and that's exactly why it's still worth finding.
hero_note: We couldn't find a freely licensed off-road photo of a first-generation Ramcharger or Trail Duster, so these photos were taken on the grass at car shows.

paragraphs: By 1974 Ford had been selling the Bronco since 1966 and Chevrolet the [[chevrolet/k5-blazer-1st|K5 Blazer]] since 1969, and Dodge had nothing to sell against them. Its answer was the Ramcharger, a Dodge pickup with the bed cut off and the wheelbase shortened by 9 inches. It arrived for the 1974 model year, and Plymouth dealers got a twin called the Trail Duster. It was late, but it came with something rare in 1974: full-time four-wheel drive as standard. You could also order a 440 big-block, and the roof was optional.

story.heading: THE RHINO
paragraphs: During development the truck was code-named 'Rhino', and the finished product lived up to the name. It used a 106-inch version of the Dodge pickup's AD platform and was assembled at Warren Truck in Michigan. Dodge sold it as a basic utility vehicle. Early trucks had only a driver's seat as standard, and Wikipedia says the passenger seat stayed on the options list until 1976. The roof was optional too. You could have no top, a dealer-fitted fabric top, or a removable steel hardtop with a flip-up rear window.

The very first trucks were stranger still. Until the June 10, 1974 build date, the door pillars were part of the removable roof, so the 'half doors' had no frame above the glass. Later trucks got normal pickup doors. The name had history too. AutoGuide notes that 'Ramchargers' had been a club of Chrysler employees who went drag racing in the 1950s, and the badge had stayed on factory-backed racing efforts ever since. A 1974 SUV with a roof that unbolted and a cooler built into the console was a fitting way to use it.

story.heading: FULL-TIME, ALL THE TIME
paragraphs: The trick was the New Process NP203 transfer case. Dodge's 1978 brochure describes five lever positions. Low Loc locks the center differential and gives a 2.0:1 low range for snow, mud and sand. Low keeps the center differential working. Neutral is for running a power take-off. High is for everyday driving, and High Loc is for extra traction. There were no front hubs to lock, because the Spicer 44 front axle was a full-time design with nothing to disengage. Consumer Guide notes that most 4x4s of the period had part-time systems, which couldn't be used on dry pavement.

The rest of the running gear was heavy-duty Dodge truck: leaf springs at both ends, a Chrysler 9¼-inch rear axle, power front disc brakes and a 36,000 psi steel frame. The 225 slant six was available, along with the 318 and 360 small-blocks and the 400 and 440 big-blocks. The 1977 brochure still lists the 440 for the four-wheel-drive AW100. A Ramcharger even won the 1975 Sno*Drift rally.

story.heading: FROM FLEET SPECIAL TO MACHO
paragraphs: Dodge added a two-wheel-drive AD100 and the slant six for 1975, according to Ramcharger Central's year-by-year notes. From there the truck grew more comfortable every year. The SE package brought cloth-and-vinyl buckets, woodgrain trim, a lockable console with a removable beverage chest and extra gauges. By 1978 you could order a three-passenger front bench, a Sky Lite sunroof, a CB radio, a factory Sno-Commander snowplow package, and towing packages for trailers of up to 6,000 lb.

For 1978 Dodge also leaned into the van-and-decals spirit of the age. The Ramcharger Four by Four came with the Macho package: bold body and tailgate graphics, spoke or chrome wheels, 10-15LT tires and power steering. Top Hand trucks with their own graphics turned up the same year. For 1979 the truck got a new hood, grille and headlights, with four rectangular lamps on the upper trims. The big-blocks were gone, leaving the 318 as standard and the 360 as the option on the 4x4.

story.heading: THE LAST OPEN-AIR DODGE
paragraphs: In 1980 Dodge dropped full-time four-wheel drive and switched to a part-time system with the chain-drive NP208. It was the generation's last year. The 1981 [[ramcharger/ramcharger-2nd|second-generation Ramcharger]] followed the redesigned Ram pickup and got a welded-on steel roof and a fiberglass liftgate. That ended the open-air era, and the Trail Duster was dropped after 1981. Rivals kept going in their own directions. The [[chevrolet/k5-blazer|square-body K5]] kept a removable rear top, and the [[bronco/full-size|full-size Bronco]], new for 1978, became the Ramcharger's most direct rival.

Today the first generation is the Ramcharger collectors want. AutoGuide says the earliest and latest Ramchargers generally bring the most money. On Bring a Trailer, Trail Dusters have recently sold for more than equivalent Dodges. Owners on Ramcharger Central still argue about the NP203. Torque King, which sells the parts, calls it troublesome. One long-time member's verdict is 'Just leave it alone! … The 203 is an awesome transfer case.' Keep the front hubs greased, and he may well be right.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE PLYMOUTH VERSION
callout.title: Trail Duster: Plymouth's only SUV
paragraphs: Plymouth's version arrived alongside the Dodge for 1974 and was sold until 1981. It was Plymouth's only SUV, and Motor1 says it was basically a Ramcharger with a different badge. DrivingLine calls it the much rarer twin. OldCarBrochures holds separate Trail Duster brochures for 1976, 1977 and 1978. The top trim was the Trail Duster Sport, and Motor1 notes its faux-wood trim.

Today the badge matters at auction. Of the 16 first-generation trucks that sold on Bring a Trailer between December 2021 and August 2026, the seven Dodges brought $15,110–26,500. The nine Trail Dusters brought $17,945–57,500, and seven of them sold for $29,000 or more.

engineering_intro: Underneath, the Ramcharger is a short-wheelbase Dodge W100 half-ton: a ladder frame with leaf springs at all four corners, a Spicer 44 front axle and a Chrysler 9¼-inch rear. From 1974 to 1979 every 4x4 had full-time four-wheel drive through the gear-and-chain NP203. The 1980 trucks went part-time with the NP208. Behind the doors you get an optional steel hardtop or nothing at all.

engineering.v: Shortened Dodge pickup ladder frame, 106 in wheelbase
engineering.note: 9 in shorter than the Ram pickup's, on Chrysler's AD platform. Dodge's 1978 brochure lists 36,000 psi steel with a 2.86 section modulus.
3,500 lb capacity on 48 x 2.5 in leaves (1977 and 1979 brochures). There are no locking hubs on the full-time axle.
3,600 lb capacity on 52 x 2.5 in leaves. Anti-spin was optional with every ratio (1979 brochure). Ratios included 3.2, 3.55 and 3.9.
The NP203 has five positions, Low Loc, Low, Neutral, High and High Loc, with a 2.0:1 low range (1978 brochure).
The 440 was 4x4-only. The big-blocks were dropped for 1979, when the 318 became standard on the AW100 and the six was limited to the 2WD AD100.

engineering.v: None, dealer soft top, or removable steel hardtop
engineering.note: The double-wall steel top has a tailgate with pneumatic assist (1978 brochure). Trucks built before June 10, 1974 have 'half doors' that rely on the roof for their window frames.

generations_table.note: Full-time NP203. The top was optional and the passenger seat cost extra. Half doors until the June 10, 1974 build date.
The 2WD model has coil-spring independent front suspension. Revised dash. On SE trucks the instrument panel adds volt and vacuum gauges.
New grille with rectangular parking lamps. The brochure lists electronic ignition on every engine. The 440 was 4x4-only.
Hurst transfer-case shifter, new towing packages and a three-passenger front bench. Last year for the big-blocks.
New hood, grille and headlights. Upper trims get four rectangular lamps. The NP203 stays.
Part-time 4WD with the NP208. Black-painted grille openings. Last year for the removable top.

buying_checks.head: Rust: wheel wells, floors and the radiator support
buying_checks.body: Ramcharger Central members list the rear wheel wells, lower sills and fenders, the bottom of the radiator support, the floors (especially the driver's side and the rear floor), the rain gutters and the windshield surround. Also look under the battery and at the bottoms of the doors. One desert truck still needed metal in the core support. Bring a magnet.

buying_checks.head: Find out which 4WD system it really has
buying_checks.body: From 1974 to 1979 the truck should have a full-time NP203 and a front axle with no hubs. If you see locking hubs, a part-time conversion kit or a different transfer case, ask what was changed. Ramcharger Central's SuperBurban warns that the NP203's park pawl only holds when the front axle is engaged or the case is in Loc. A converted truck with unlocked hubs can roll away in Park.

buying_checks.head: Shake the front wheels
buying_checks.body: On a forum thread about a full-time 1978 Dodge, one experienced owner calls the full-time front hub bearings 'the weak spot in these trucks from day one'. They were sealed for life until a grease fitting was added in 1976, and few owners ever greased them. Jack up each front wheel and rock it top to bottom. You want zero play. Wide tires on big-offset wheels wear these bearings faster.

buying_checks.head: Steering box mount and wander
buying_checks.body: Ramcharger Central members say the stock steering box mounting plate is prone to cracking. Dodge made the plate thicker in 1988, and members recommend the 1977–93 box design as an upgrade for earlier trucks. Check for cracks around the box and the frame rail, and for wandering steering. NHTSA's 1978 recalls covered the intermediate shaft's pot coupling and a misindexed lower shaft, so ask whether the recall work was done.

buying_checks.head: Is the engine the one it was born with?
buying_checks.body: These trucks get re-engined constantly. Bring a Trailer has sold first-gen trucks with 340, 383 and 408 V8s, a Cummins 6BT and even a 1974 Trail Duster body on a 1992 Ramcharger chassis. A window sticker or build sheet is gold. The 440 was 4x4-only, the six wasn't sold in California, and the big-blocks were gone after 1978.

buying_checks.head: Big-block heat
buying_checks.body: A 440 in a short truck runs hot. The seller of a 1976 Ramcharger on BaT reported overheating at idle in hot weather. A Ramcharger Central member with a 440 trail truck fought constant overheating and low oil pressure at high rpm until he pulled the engine. Look for an upgraded radiator, a working fan shroud and a temperature gauge that stays put in traffic.

buying_checks.head: The roof, the doors and their seals
buying_checks.body: Make sure a removable hardtop is actually there and fits. A truck built before June 10, 1974 with half doors needs its matching roof, because the door pillars are part of it. Hardtop rear-glass weatherstrip is a known chore. Ramcharger Central members use the factory rope trick or work it in with stiff plastic.

buying_checks.head: Odometers and titles
buying_checks.body: Five-digit odometers roll over, and many BaT listings describe true mileage as unknown. Read the title too. Listings have shown Classic and 'Exceeds Limits' brands, and liens. Service records and original paperwork are worth real money in this market.

repairs.title: Grease the full-time front hub bearings
repairs.symptoms: Play when you rock a raised front wheel top to bottom, or noise from the front hubs. Neglect is the main cause: from 1976 the bearings have a grease fitting that most owners never found.
repairs.fix: These are the steps SuperBurban gives on Ramcharger Central. Jack up one front wheel and take it off. Look through the holes around the wheel studs with a flashlight and rotate the hub until you find the grease fitting. Give it several pumps from a grease gun. While the wheel is off the ground, shake it from top to bottom. There should be no play at all. If there is, plan on new bearings or a hub assembly. Grease both sides about once a year. Keep wheel offset close to stock, because big-offset wheels load these closely spaced bearings unevenly.
repairs.tools: Floor jack and stands · lug wrench · flashlight · grease gun with a needle or angled coupler

parts.name: Wheel bearing and hub parts, 1978 Ramcharger

repairs.title: Service and reseal the NP203 transfer case
repairs.time: ≈ 1 hour for a fluid change; a reseal takes much longer
repairs.cost: Torque King's NP203 gasket and seal kit is $59.98
repairs.symptoms: Oil dripping from the case or the output seals, a low fluid level, or a chain that has worn noisy. One forum veteran says the 203 is 'perfectly adequate and strong if the chain and sprockets are not worn out'.
repairs.fix: Torque King's Dodge transfer case chart, compiled from factory shop manuals, calls for SAE 10W-30 engine oil in the 1974–79 Ramcharger's NP203, with a capacity of 9 pints. Drain it, check the magnet and fluid for metal, and refill to the fill plug. If it's weeping, reseal the case with a gasket and seal kit, following the factory shop manual. A bearing kit is available if the case comes apart. If it seeps after a switch to synthetic oil, Torque King points out that old seals may not like the additives, so reseal it first.
repairs.tools: Drain pan · socket set · fluid pump · seal puller and drivers · factory shop manual

parts.name: NP203 bearing, seal and gasket kit (QU52338)
Small parts kit for 1973–79 NP203 full-time cases (QU50294)

repairs.title: Convert the NP203 to part-time
repairs.symptoms: Not a fault, just a choice. Owners convert for less driveline drag and wear on the road. Ramcharger Central is split: some say the fuel savings don't justify it, and others just leave the case in High Loc.
repairs.fix: Mile Marker's 203 Conversion Kit (PN 501) replaces the NP203's internal differential parts with a wedged-gear assembly, so the case works like a part-time unit. It installs with common tools, according to Mile Marker. Pull the case, follow the kit instructions and reseal it as you go. Then decide what to do with the front axle. SuperBurban says a full-time axle can stay as it is and simply turn with the front driveshaft. If you add locking hubs, remember that the 203's park pawl needs the front axle engaged, so fit drive flanges or leave the hubs locked. One forum veteran calls hub conversions for half-ton Dodges expensive and not very strong. Swapping in a 1981-or-later front axle is the alternative.
repairs.tools: Transmission jack · socket set · snap-ring pliers · torque wrench · kit instructions

parts.name: NP203 gasket and seal kit for reassembly (QU50371)

repairs.title: Reinforce the steering box mount
repairs.symptoms: Wandering steering, a steering box that moves when someone turns the wheel with the engine running, or cracks around the box mounting plate or the frame rail.
repairs.fix: First find the actual cause. Ramcharger Central members point out that worn couplers and loose parts cause wander too, and a pot-coupler rebuild kit is available. If the plate is cracked, replace it. Dodge's thicker 1988 plate is discontinued, but Autofab builds a heavy-duty bolt-on version for 1972–93 trucks. Far From Stock's brace works with the stock plate on 1976–93 trucks that keep stock 4x4 steering. On 1974–76 trucks with the early reverse-rotation box, members suggest the 1977–93 box and its parts as a straight swap. Weld any frame cracks before you add a brace.
repairs.tools: Socket set · torque wrench · pitman-arm puller · welder if the frame is cracked

parts.name: 1972–93 Dodge 4x4 / Ramcharger steering box mounting bracket

repairs.title: Replace the Dana 44 inner axle seals
repairs.cost: Torque King's seal kits with installer are $189.50–194.50
repairs.symptoms: A front differential that keeps running low, or gear oil working its way out toward the steering knuckles.
repairs.fix: Remove the front hubs and spindles and pull the axle shafts, then remove the old inner seals from the axle tubes. Torque King's application chart lists the seals by build date. Trucks from 1974 to early 1977 (axle BOM 603036, and 603790 on the W100) use seal QU40055. Late-1977 to 1980 Ramchargers and Trail Dusters use QU40159. Use an installer that sets each seal to the correct depth. Torque King's adjustable tool also lets you move the seal lip onto an unworn part of the shaft. Refill the differential and check the knuckle seals and bearings while everything is apart.
repairs.tools: Hub and spindle sockets · slide hammer or seal puller · inner seal installer · gear oil and pump

parts.name: QK4872 Dana 44 inner axle seal kit with adjustable-depth tool (1974–early 1977)
QK4830 inner axle seal kit for 1970s–80s Dana 44 (late 1977–1980)

repairs.title: Sort out a hot-running big-block
repairs.symptoms: The temperature climbs at idle or in traffic on hot days. One BaT seller and one Ramcharger Central member both reported it on 440 trucks.
repairs.fix: Start with the cheap things. Pressure-test the system and replace the cap, the hoses and the 50-year-old coolant. Make sure the fan shroud is present and the fan clutch actually locks up. If the radiator is original and partly blocked, many owners fit an aluminum radiator. Several of the trucks sold on BaT have them, including a 440 SE and a Top Hand. Check the ignition timing too. If it's still hot, look at the water pump and thermostat before blaming the engine.
repairs.tools: Cooling-system pressure tester · infrared thermometer · basic hand tools

parts.name: Radiators, fan clutches, hoses and thermostats, 1978 Ramcharger

repairs.title: Patch rust at the quarters, floors and core support
repairs.cost: Mill Supply's 1974 lower rear quarter kit is $178.28
repairs.symptoms: Bubbles in the rear wheel arches and rockers, soft floors, a wet driver's door sill after rain, or a radiator support crumbling at the bottom.
repairs.fix: Cut out back to clean metal and butt-weld in repair sections, then seam-seal and coat the inside. One Ramcharger Central member traced a wet door sill to an open body seam just below the driver's window and cured it with body seal compound. Another patched a rotted lower core support with a screwed-on aluminum strip. Mill Supply lists 27 repair parts for 1974–80 Ramchargers, including quarter panel, bed-floor and rocker sections.
repairs.tools: Cut-off wheel · MIG welder · panel clamps · seam sealer · rust converter and cavity wax

parts.name: 1974–80 Dodge Ramcharger repair panels (quarters, floors, rockers, wheel arches)

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: Dodge's largest factory option was a 10-15LT, which the 1978 Macho package used. On Bring a Trailer, listings that mention no lift mostly show 31x10.50R15s. One Top Hand truck ran 32x11.50s, and a 1978 Trail Duster sold on 33x12.50R15s. On a later Ramcharger with the same Dana 44 and leaf-spring layout, an owner found 32x11.50s rubbed when the suspension twisted up. So call 31s safe and 32s the practical limit, and plan on an add-a-leaf or lift before you try 33s off-road.

faq.q: What's the difference between a Ramcharger and a Trail Duster?
faq.a: The badge and the trim. Motor1 calls the Trail Duster basically a Ramcharger with a different badge. Plymouth sold it from 1974 to 1981, and it was Plymouth's only SUV. It's the rarer of the two, and on Bring a Trailer Trail Dusters have recently sold for more than comparable Dodges.

faq.q: Is the full-time NP203 a problem?
faq.a: Opinions differ. Torque King calls it 'troublesome', and many trucks were converted to part-time. Ramcharger Central members mostly defend it. They say it's heavy but durable, with a usable low range, and one argues that its poor fuel-economy reputation really comes from the weak late-1970s engines it was paired with. Keep the chain and fluid healthy and grease the front hubs. Mile Marker's PN 501 kit converts it to part-time if you'd rather.
faq.src: TORQUE KING · RAMCHARGER CENTRAL · MILE MARKER

faq.q: Does the roof really come off?
faq.a: Yes, on every 1974–80 truck. You could buy one with no top, a dealer-installed vinyl soft top with roll-up windows, or the removable double-wall steel hardtop. Trucks built before June 10, 1974 have half doors whose window frames are part of the roof. The 1981 second generation got a welded-on steel roof.

The 225 slant six (2WD only from 1979, and never sold in California) and the 318 and 360 small-blocks. The 400 and 440 big-blocks lasted through 1978, and the 440 was 4x4-only. The 1974 trucks were V8-only, according to Ramcharger Central and Consumer Guide's reading of the launch ad. From 1979 the 318 was standard on the 4x4, with the 360 optional.

faq.q: What does the NP203 take, and how much?
faq.a: SAE 10W-30 engine oil, 9 pints, for the 1974–79 Ramcharger. That's according to Torque King's chart, compiled from factory shop manuals. A 1980 truck with the part-time NP208 takes Dexron III or ATF+4, 6 pints.

Dodge's 1978 brochure offered a standard towing package for trailers under 2,000 lb gross, with a 7-inch-section step bumper and a 1⅞-inch ball. The optional heavy-duty package with a load-equalizing hitch covered trailers up to 6,000 lb gross. The 1979 AW100 was rated at 6,050 lb GVW.

faq.q: What axles and gears does it have?
faq.a: A Spicer 44 front, rated at 3,500 lb on the 4x4, and a Chrysler 9¼-inch rear rated at 3,600 lb. Brochures list 3.2, 3.55 and 3.9 ratios, and Dodge says anti-spin was available with every ratio. A 1978 Macho sold on BaT left the factory with 3.55s, a limited-slip rear and the 35-gallon tank.

faq.q: How big is the fuel tank?
faq.a: 24 gallons as standard and 35 gallons as an option, according to the 1977 and 1978 brochures.

Yes. For 1980 Dodge switched the 4x4s from full-time to part-time four-wheel drive with the chain-drive NP208, and painted the grille openings black. Sources disagree on whether the locking-hub front end with the 5-on-5.5 bolt pattern arrived for 1980 or 1981, so check the truck itself. A 1980 Ramcharger also has an NHTSA campaign (84V115) that adds a fuel-tank skid plate.

On Bring a Trailer, 16 first-generation trucks sold between December 2021 and August 2026 for $15,110 to $57,500, with a median of about $27,750. The seven Dodges sold for $15,110–26,500. Most Trail Dusters brought $29,000–42,250, and a 340-powered Trail Duster Sport reached $57,500.

baseline_service.intro: Assume every fluid is old and every rubber part is original until you've seen receipts. The first generation has two jobs most owners forget: greasing the full-time front hubs, and the NP203's oil fill, which takes engine oil, not gear oil. We couldn't verify most factory capacities, so check them against the Dodge factory service manual for your year.

items.interval: Now, then every 3,000–5,000 mi [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Find out which engine is actually in it first. 340, 383, 408 and diesel swaps are common.

items.spec: Plug gap and timing [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: By 1977 Dodge's brochure lists electronic ignition on every engine. Some owners have since fitted GM HEI distributors.

items.spec: Coolant type and capacity [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Big-blocks run hot in this short engine bay, and aluminum radiators are a common retrofit.

items.interval: Change now, then at the manual's interval
items.note: From Torque King's chart, compiled from factory shop manuals. 1980 trucks with the NP208 take Dexron III or ATF+4, 6 pints. If the old seals start weeping after a switch to synthetic oil, reseal the case first.

items.interval: Now, then about once a year
items.note: From 1976 there's a grease fitting hidden behind the hub. Look through the holes around the wheel studs. Check for play while the wheel is off the ground.

items.note: If the level keeps dropping, suspect the inner axle seals. The seal part number changed partway through 1977.

items.note: Look for cracks at the box mount. On 1978 trucks, ask whether the steering-shaft recalls were done.
On 50-year-old trucks, the fuel lines, the vent lines and the tank sending unit are all due. One BaT SE had all three replaced. Check for the optional 35-gallon tank.
